body:
https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/992 makes UrlProtocol host shutdown complete even when a full native event-loop queue rejects close work. Its review, R992, raised finding 5, and lane F992b confirmed it: in jvm-libp2p snapshot-41, `PlainNettyTransport.close()` reaches its private acceptor event-loop group shutdown only through `allClosed.thenCompose`. When any listener close fails, that stage is skipped and the acceptor loop is never shut down.

Owned TCP/WebSocket acceptor shutdown and QUIC worker shutdown now run after channel close succeeds or fails. The returned future retains the original channel failure after cleanup, and caller completion or cancellation cannot stop that private cleanup. TCP/WebSocket shared workers remain available to other transports.

FLIBP6 rebased this PR onto current `develop` (base 436997d5e5f5b80f1503504b19e5b813654a3a49). The current PR head is [23d66d4110465edb1ae8d83e099266a42ae77f41](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/23d66d4110465edb1ae8d83e099266a42ae77f41). Current develop still has success-only group cleanup; the change is not superseded. The Kotlin-to-Groovy build-file migration was resolved by carrying the version declaration into current `build.gradle`.

The existing publication is `community.kotlin.libp2p:jvm-libp2p:1.3.0-codexcoder21-snapshot-42`, built from [775bfeb68e566f8a4b3ed3eb90e797752127d5de](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/775bfeb68e566f8a4b3ed3eb90e797752127d5de). Its downloaded JAR hash is `9b97f80c185b5c4b344b88e834c1fac09979651ba7e91a6ec020f6a438db7972`; a fresh exact-source build has hash `7724ca1a14579a96063eff52aecb1fe44ebff7c02d25bafb001d8a08c20ea6d6`. All 1,011 entries and the POM match, and zeroing only ZIP timestamp fields makes the archives identical. The brief requires a raw-hash match, so the one authorized replacement uses snapshot-45; 43 and 44 already exist and both 45 endpoints returned 404. **Snapshot-45 has not been published.**

Fresh validation: the old-product control on current develop has 11/11 adverse cases failing at the owned-group termination assertion, with both success controls passing (13 cases, zero errors/skips). The unchanged original 54-case adjacent register passes 54/54, one native JUnit attempt per case, using the successfully compiled fixed classes and an immutable runtime snapshot. A later test compile stopped on warnings in two additional PR-only coverage fixtures; those warnings were corrected, and the expanded 15-case red / 56-case green register and packaging are queued for shared JVM slots. Those new coverage files are preserved in evidence and are not claimed as passing.

The required repository check is `bld-build`; its Actions run on this head is pending assessment. The informational remote checks are not the full-suite verdict for this lane. The consumer candidate and 30x gates still require the verified release, so [UrlProtocol](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/992) remains not ready.

Existing-main test edits: none. No timeout, iteration count or assertion was weakened. No merge, enqueue, close, deployment or check rerun was performed.

[FLIBP6 evidence, native XML, archive hashes and review](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/tree/wip/FLIBP6-evidence-20261104/evidence/FLIBP6).


FLIBP6 cutoff result: the expanded old-product control has 13 intended group-termination failures and two passing controls. The fixed expanded register is 55/56: `QuicTransportFailedConnectionSetTest.oneOutboundCloseFailureStillClosesEveryConnectionAndUdpParent` fails because a client UDP parent's close future does not settle after its event-loop group terminates. This is before fixture cleanup. Physical open/registered state remains to be measured. Publication is withheld; no snapshot-45 release or consumer repeat gate is claimed. The new reproducer and complete native XML are in the FLIBP6 evidence branch.
